leads.summary: The new shell guard reports success when none of the three Variants uses the filtered model
leads.consequence: rg -c emits no stdout and exits 1 on zero matches; substituting its empty stdout yields an arithmetic syntax error in the if condition, which Bash treats as false. The test prints its success line after the if. For example, replacing all three model expressions with model: root.unfilteredScreens while leaving the realScreens property and BarModel tests intact evades this guard. This is a false negative in the regression test, not a demonstrated runtime defect in the current Bar.qml.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (N1, folded into F2); corroboration; published

leads.summary: Open PR #6501's bar.screens feature conflicts with this PR's three model bindings
leads.consequence: Both PRs change the same three Variants and both tests require their own model name. Keeping #6501's root.barScreens in the merged QML bypasses this PR's placeholder/FALLBACK filter when barConfig.screens is absent or empty; keeping only root.realScreens loses #6501's user-configured monitor allowlist. Even if the textual merge is resolved, the two source guards conflict until the filters are composed and their test expectations updated. #6501 currently reports mergeable_state=dirty, so this is an integration warning, not a bug in this PR alone.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (N3); corroboration; published as Related PR note

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Follow-up on [the earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13165#issuecomment-5823447346) and [the author's reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13165#issuecomment-5833645859), checked at `f98b5554`.

**Verified:** No functional issue found in the new commit. The code-comment finding is resolved. The optional test note is mostly resolved: one mutation it described still passes, now because of a small arithmetic check, with a one-line fix below.

| Earlier item | Outcome at `f98b5554` |
|---|---|
| Code comment overstates what is tracked | Resolved |
| Optional test improvement | Mostly resolved; all three `Variants` pointed at another unfiltered list still passes (below) |
| Earlier **Verified** items (filter shapes, all three `Variants` filtered, delegate reuse, test fails on `quattro`) | Still hold |

**Verified:** The new `Bar.qml` comment matches Qt Wayland 6.11.2: a screen gets a default `Screen%1` name at construction, is named from the output events before initialization, and is added only once initialized. Only its geometry can arrive late.

**Verified:** Moving the filter into `BarModel.js` keeps the binding reactive. `Bar.qml` imports `BarModel.js` (no `.pragma library`), and qtdeclarative captures non-constant property reads (here width and height) made inside a called function for the whole binding evaluation. A sandboxed `qml6 --apptype core` probe with this head's `BarModel.js` and stand-in screen objects re-evaluated when a 0x0 `HDMI-A-1` got its size, when the list changed, and when a screen's width went to 0.

**Verified:** The new Node checks fail when `FALLBACK` or the placeholder is let through, when the size check is removed, or when `realScreens` skips the filter. The full `bar-test.sh` passes on this head (97 checks) and fails on `quattro` at the first new check. An equivalent reordering of the guard now passes.

### Count check passes when nothing matches

`test/shell.d/bar-test.sh:28` puts `rg -c` straight into arithmetic:

```bash
if (( $(rg -c 'model:\s*root\.realScreens' "$ROOT/shell/plugins/bar/Bar.qml") != 3 )); then
```

With zero matches, `rg -c` prints nothing, so bash evaluates `(( != 3 ))`. That is an arithmetic syntax error with status 1. The `if` skips `fail`, and `set -e` does not apply inside an `if` condition. In a sandboxed run, pointing all three `Variants` at a new `allScreens: Quickshell.screens` property (with `realScreens` left defined) passed the whole file: exit 0, 97 `ok` lines, and only `((: != 3 : arithmetic syntax error` on stderr. One or two `Variants` moved off the filter are still caught, and so is pointing all three straight at `Quickshell.screens` (the first check).

**Impact:** Test-only. Runtime filtering is correct on this head, but the check meant to guard all three surfaces cannot fail when all three use another list.

**Suggested change:** Compare as strings, so an empty count fails:

```bash
if [[ $(rg -c 'model:\s*root\.realScreens' "$ROOT/shell/plugins/bar/Bar.qml") != 3 ]]; then
```

In the same sandbox, this head still passes with the change, and the all-three mutation fails with `not ok - bar, drag ghost and move ghost surfaces must all use the real-screen filter`.

**Comment note:** `BarModel.js:160-161` says "The size check matters for the placeholder only". The empty-name test already rejects the placeholder, so the size check matters for a named screen whose geometry has not arrived yet (the `unsized` DP-1 case in the tests).

**Related PR:** Open #6501 rewrites the same three `Variants` to `root.barScreens` (built from unfiltered `Quickshell.screens`) and adds exports to the same `BarModel.js` block. Its test requires three `model: root.barScreens`. Whichever lands second needs to compose the two filters and reconcile both source checks.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Follow-up source review of `f98b5554` against the earlier reviewed head `0fd2e550`, plus Quickshell 0.3.1, qtdeclarative and qtbase 6.11.2 and Hyprland 0.56.2 source. Sandboxed runs covered the full `bar-test.sh` on head with Node, the updated test on base, 10 mutation cases, the string-comparison fix, and a core-mode QML binding probe using stand-in screens. The `Variants` delegate-reuse item was rechecked by source only. No live compositor, KVM or hardware reproduction.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.
